entries.notes: Single author, workshop. Strong design: identical Hermes harness, default system prompt, identical tool schemas and fixed sampling across four models, matched no-shift control branches, one-at-a-time harness manipulations and replication on a second harness; code released. Conclusions 0.5: n=16 prefixes per model and n=4-8 for replications, which the author states, so the effect claims outrun the sample.

entries.title: The Interplay of Harness Design and Post-Training in LLM Agents
entries.notes: Factorial over harness informativeness x model size x RL algorithm x tool schema on one environment with every cell reported, including the post-hoc-application and schema-shift arms that expose a harness-overfitting failure mode. Single-environment and two-model scope stated. Artifacts 0.

entries.title: Harness Engineering for Language Agents: The Harness Layer as Control, Agency, and Runtime
entries.notes: Preprints.org position paper. Baseline 0.5 and metrics 0.5: a lightweight descriptive audit of 40 works with interpretive, non-exclusive tags, which the authors call a visibility check rather than a bibliometric result. Conclusions 0.5: openly concedes it supplies no causal evidence for its own thesis. Six explicit limitations.

entries.title: The A-R Behavioral Space: Execution-Level Profiling of Tool-Using Language Model Agents in Organizational Deployment
entries.notes: Model, prompts, tool schemas, sandbox and decoding fixed with only reasoning-scaffold depth varied, and the direction of the effect differs across models rather than being reported uniformly. Conclusions 0.5: cells are n=10-30, so the 60-90 point execution-rate swings rest on small denominators. Artifacts 0.

entries.title: LLM Agents for Interactive Workflow Provenance: Reference Architecture and Evaluation Methodology
entries.notes: Runs both halves: model fixed while a six-step context ladder is added, then context fixed while five models are swapped, with two judge families cross-checking. Metrics 0.5: a 20-query author-curated golden set scored by LLM judges. Flowcept code released. Venue 0.5: workshop.

entries.title: Advancing LLM Agents for Code Generation: Observability, Orchestration, Reliable Performance
entries.notes: LOW. Single-author conference paper. Design 0.5, baseline 0.5 and metrics 0.5: success rates are reported per retry index for each model pairing with no sample size, no repetitions and no statistics, the task set is described only as 'LeetCode problems', and the ReAct comparison flow is asserted to be error-prone but never measured. Threats 0.5: no limitations section, only scattered caveats. Conclusions 0.5: configuration rankings drawn from single runs. Artifacts 0.

entries.title: Harnessing LLMs for Reliable Academic Supervision: A Comparative Study
entries.notes: Single author, but a genuine 2x2 model-by-harness factorial with blind raters, an adversarial assignment placing the stronger model in the thin baseline, and paired Wilcoxon tests. Conclusions 0.5: inter-rater agreement is very weak (Fleiss kappa 0.10-0.11, mean weighted Cohen kappa 0.30) yet a strong harness-dominates conclusion is drawn; the authors disclose this and retain an outlier rater for honesty. Artifacts 0.5: architecture described as released, no resolvable link.

entries.title: First head-to-head comparison of agentic AI applied to the analysis of simulated data of the Einstein Telescope
entries.notes: LOW-MODERATE. Single author, two runs. Design 0.5 and baseline 0.5: the compared units are two whole commercial agent products, and the author states they used different underlying models for the manuscript step, so quality differences may reflect model capability as much as agent implementation; there is no independent reference implementation. Metrics 0.5: behavioural counts with no statistics at n=2. Artifacts 0: personal website link only.

entries.title: Bounded Returns to Orchestration: A Synthesis Ceiling Beneath Eleven Controlled Deep-Research Architectures
entries.notes: Single-author Zenodo deposit but the most carefully controlled attribution study of the topology set: one model, one tool layer, one retry policy across eleven architectures, a reliability-audited three-judge cross-family panel, plus report-length adjustment, token-budget clamping, a local 7B twin, an RL-trained control and a best-of-N control. The headline is a deflationary null applied to its own effect, and the unequalised compute budget and Krippendorff alpha of 0.42 are disclosed. Venue 0: not peer reviewed.

entries.title: Harness Engineering for Agentic AI Coding Tools: An Exploratory Study
entries.notes: Repository-mining study of 2,853 projects filtered from 37,249, with detection heuristics validated by an AI-authored-commit scan and clear counts. Baseline 0: descriptive mining with no comparison condition, which the authors are explicit about, framing the contribution as descriptive rather than causal. Artifacts 0.5: 'data are available online' via a citation.

entries.title: Baselines Before Architecture: Evaluating Coding Agents for Autonomous Penetration Testing
entries.notes: Three-phase design isolating one factor at a time (scaffold at fixed model, prompt at fixed agent and model, model generation at fixed scaffold) with matched budget, target interface and scoring, paired McNemar tests, and explicit labelling of the MAPTA and PentestGPT rows as descriptive comparisons against published results rather than ablations. Artifacts 0.

entries.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
entries.notes: Base model fixed while the harness is evolved, with output-token, cost and cache accounting used to rule out inference-scaling explanations. Metrics 0.5: outcomes are pairwise LLM-as-a-judge comparisons on 30 synthetic tasks with no absolute measure. Conclusions 0.5: the opus-4.7 arm is admitted inconclusive on the token confound and the implicit-objective evidence is admitted correlational. Artifacts 0.

entries.title: BioML-bench: Evaluation of AI Agents for End-to-End Biomedical ML
entries.notes: Design 0.5 and conclusions 0.5: each agent runs its own recommended LLM backend (GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4, an OpenRouter default), so scaffold and model are confounded across arms, yet the paper concludes that architecture and scaffolding are the primary drivers of capability. The authors name this confound in their limitations, which is why threats scores 1. Dummy-agent floor and human leaderboard percentiles are good controls. Artifacts 0.

entries.title: Automating agentic collaborative ontology engineering with role-playing simulation of LLM-powered agents and RAG technology
entries.notes: Knowledge Engineering Review journal; component-level ablation of a retrieval-and-guidance harness around a fixed LLM with a bare-LLM control and a human reference ontology, and candid about non-monotonic effects. Design 0.5 and conclusions 0.5: single run per setting with no repetition or statistics, and the striking cross-model spread (78% versus 10.2% versus 0.9%) comes from one exploratory run.

entries.title: SWEnergy: An Empirical Study on Energy Efficiency in Agentic Issue Resolution Frameworks with SLMs
entries.notes: Model, hardware, timeout, context window and benchmark held constant with only the framework varied, 1,200 runs, hardware-level RAPL/NVML instrumentation and code released. Conclusions 0.5: task resolution is 0-4% in every configuration, so only the energy findings carry signal and the accuracy-side statements have essentially no discriminating power.

entries.title: Echoing: Identity Failures when LLM Agents Talk to Each Other
entries.notes: Design 0.5: deliberately asymmetric, 22 customer models against only 3 seller configurations, with echoing detected by an LLM judge; the authors state both. The schema-level mitigation is otherwise a clean fixed-model, fixed-tool, fixed-budget manipulation. Artifacts 0. Venue 0.5: workshop.

entries.title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
entries.notes: Factorially separates monitor scaffolding from monitor information with monitor LLM, dataset and threat model fixed, 20 rollouts across 32 tasks, human baselines, and code, dataset and logs released; offline-only scope and prompted rather than trained attackers both disclosed.

entries.title: BrowseComp-Plus: A More Fair and Transparent Evaluation Benchmark of Deep-Research Agent
entries.notes: Purpose-built to remove a harness confound: a fixed human-verified 100k-document corpus lets retriever and agent be varied independently, with a BM25 common baseline and an oracle upper bound. Quantifies its own 512-token truncation cost (13.5% of queries lose the answer) and documents the 830-of-1,266 query attrition. Full release.

entries.title: A Survey of LLM-based Automated Program Repair: Taxonomies, Design Paradigms, and Applications
entries.notes: Systematic survey with independently double-coded paradigms (kappa 0.97-0.98) and a comparability audit at the level of individual reported results, which is what makes its 'exactly one model-controlled pair out of 2,145' finding credible. Baseline 0.5: comparison windows are defined but there is no experimental baseline, by design. Curated repository released.

entries.title: FHIR-AgentBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Realistic Interoperable EHR Question Answering
entries.notes: Controlled ablation over three harness axes on a fixed benchmark, prompt family and 32k context budget, four models, retrieval precision and recall reported alongside correctness, LLM judge validated at 97% agreement on 500 manually reviewed samples, dataset and code released, accepted at a conference.

entries.title: Harness-G: A Graph-Structured Harness for Search Agents
entries.notes: The transition-matched control is exemplary, fixing feasible targets, transitions, budgets, corpora, reward, seeds and data order. But baseline 0.5 and conclusions 0.5: the authors state that main-table baseline values are published cross-stack references and only the interface and credit ablation arms are protocol-matched, so the headline +10.74 F1 over Graph-R1 is not a matched comparison. Artifacts 0: no repository located.

entries.title: WebPilot: A Versatile and Autonomous Multi-Agent System for Web Task Execution with Strategic Exploration
entries.notes: Design 0.5 and conclusions 0.5: the headline 93% relative gain over LM-Tree Search and the lead over SteP are whole-stack comparisons in which orchestration, prompting strategy and demonstration budget differ simultaneously (4 high-level versus 10 action-level demonstrations); only the internal ablations and the GPT-3.5-to-GPT-4o swap are controlled. Threats 0.5: limitations concern the LLM and environment, not the paper's own comparisons. Artifacts 0.

entries.title: When is Tree Search Useful for LLM Planning? It Depends on the Discriminator
entries.notes: Generator LLM, sampling budget and prompts held fixed while planning method and discriminator are varied one factor at a time, with an oracle-discriminator sweep, McNemar tests and a clean demonstration that changing only the discriminator's environmental feedback improves end-to-end accuracy. Code and data released; scope limitations stated.

entries.title: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?
entries.notes: Runs both halves of the attribution experiment on the same 113-case benchmark: model pinned while the scaffold changes, then scaffold pinned while three models are swapped, with professional-tester verdicts as ground truth, four validity threats discussed and the PinATA implementation released. Journal (PACMSE).

entries.title: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research
entries.notes: One agent implementation, observation space and action space held fixed across six models and eight benchmark settings, with the usually hidden harness details (four-retry parse policy, action set, prompt shrinking, prompting flags) documented; confronts its own cross-checkpoint comparison and raises contamination. AgentLab and BrowserGym released.

entries.title: CORE-Bench: Fostering the Credibility of Published Research Through a Computational Reproducibility Agent Benchmark
entries.notes: Full 2x2 over agent scaffold and model at a fixed per-task cost limit, which is what makes the asymmetric scaffold effect interpretable; discloses that AutoGPT was run once per configuration against CORE-Agent's three, and that the corpus is restricted to already-reproducible capsules. Benchmark and code released.

entries.title: AblationBench: Evaluating Automated Planning of Ablations in Empirical AI Research
entries.notes: Same frontier models under two scaffoldings for both the planner and the judge role, with a human baseline and a trajectory-length check; reports a clean negative for scaffold complexity. Threats 0.5: only two brief limitations, both about the judge. Artifacts 0: no own repository located. Venue 0.5: workshop.

entries.title: Evaluation-Driven Development and Operations of LLM Agents: A Process Model and Reference Architecture
entries.notes: Multivocal literature review over 134 academic and 27 grey sources with academic-versus-grey strata acting as the comparison, clearly defined coding dimensions and counts, and explicit acknowledgement that validation is analytical and instantiation-based rather than experimental. Baseline 0.5: conceptual baselines only. Artifacts 0.

entries.title: mABC: multi-Agent Blockchain-Inspired Collaboration for root cause analysis in micro-services architecture
entries.notes: SERIOUS INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY. The narrative claims MABC achieves 'an average score of 64.9' and that the Decision Tree, TraceAnomaly and MEPFL baselines score 'ranging from 16.0 to 26.7', but the paper's own Table 4 gives MABC with GPT-4-Turbo an average of 46.9 and those three baselines averages of 31.6, 22.0 and 30.7 (range 22.0-31.6). The discrepancy runs in the paper's favour in both directions and roughly doubles the apparent margin; it is never flagged or corrected, so conclusions_supported is 0 and objectivity is 0. Metrics 0.5: RA/PA defined but no repetitions, variance or significance. Threats 0.5: generic scalability and data-quality remarks, no threats-to-validity section and no mention of the discrepancy. Design 0.5: the model-pinned ablation is sound, but the external ReAct comparison bundles a seven-role workflow, a 20-step cap, tool access and a re-answer retry loop against a bare ReAct.

entries.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
entries.notes: Every manual and automated method executed with the same GPT-4o-mini on the same split, so the reported spread is attributable to workflow structure; includes cross-executor transfer experiments and reports that an automated scaffold (ADAS) falls below plain IO prompting. Threats 0.5: no dedicated limitations section, though search-space and scope constraints are stated. Code released; conference publication.
